events.title: The death of Pope Clement IV
events.shortBlurb: The French lawyer-pope who counseled Aquinas and Roger Bacon died at Viterbo, and there began the longest conclave the Church has ever known…
body: Gui Foucois, called Guy le Gros, was a married advocate and trusted councillor of St. Louis IX of France. After his wife's death he took holy orders, rose to be bishop of Le Puy, archbishop of Narbonne, and cardinal of Sabina, and was elected pope at Perugia on 5 February 1265, taking the name Clement IV.

He supported Charles of Anjou against the last of the Hohenstaufen, whose cause fell at the battle of Tagliacozzo in 1268, and he was a patron of learning: he protected Thomas Aquinas and urged Roger Bacon to compose his Opus Maius on the sciences. He resided throughout his reign at Viterbo, where he died on 29 November 1268 and was buried at the Dominican church of Santa Maria in Gradi.

The cardinals, divided between French and imperial parties, could not agree on a successor. The Roman see stood vacant for one thousand and six days, until the exasperated people of Viterbo locked the electors in the palace and, it is said, stripped off its roof to hasten them. Gregory X was chosen in 1271, and the scandal gave rise to the law of the enclosed conclave — the cardinals shut up "cum clave," under key.
